title: Structure and evolution-guided design of minimal RNA-guided nucleases.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Opened the Zenodo record (4 files, CC-BY-4.0, open) and downloaded + extracted the 7.0 MB SynTnpB-1.0.0.tar.gz (41 files). Counted sequences myself: the two design files hold 10,000 sequences each, all exactly 408 amino acids, with headers that carry only a design-condition name and an index (no activity value). Reference_for_mapping.fasta holds exactly 9 constructs (1,112 nucleotides each). SynTnpB_HEK293T_plasmids.zip holds 11 files = SynTnpB v1-v9 plus wild-type ISDra2 plus one guide-RNA plasmid. masks_nuc.fasta and masks_rec.fasta hold 54 design masks each. Xiang_2023_TAM_TnpB_apc.csv is a headerless 413x413 numeric matrix (a coevolution coupling matrix), not labels. tnpb_mining/GTDB_1521_hits.faa holds 1,501 natural TnpB homologue sequences. I read map_nanopore.py: it writes a CSV with exactly two columns, 'reference' and 'count', one row per reference sequence. I found no activity, enrichment or editing-efficiency table anywhere in the deposit.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Only the abstract was retrievable. The full text is subscription-only: Europe PMC returned HTTP 500 for the full-text XML and the supplementary-files endpoint returned the explicit error 'Article with id PMC13547106 is not open access one', so the supplementary tables and the Methods (which contain the enrichment equation) could not be retrieved. Claims about screening in bacterial, plant and human cells, and the cryo-electron microscopy structure, rest on the abstract alone. I did not download the 2.12 GB nanopore_ccdb_data.fastq.zip (raw sequencing data, excluded by policy).

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 19600914 is open under CC-BY-4.0 and the 7.0 MB code/data tarball downloaded and extracted on the first try. No login or application needed.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAILS, verified in the files. There is no activity column anywhere. The only label-bearing data is the 2.12 GB raw nanopore read file; to get an activity number you must map reads with minimap2 via the authors' script to obtain per-construct read counts, then apply an enrichment equation that lives in the Methods, which is behind the subscription paywall and could not be retrieved. The 20,000 designed sequences in the two FASTA files are completely unlabelled.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are genuinely present: 20,000 full-length designed protein sequences (408 amino acids each) plus 1,501 natural TnpB homologue sequences, as literal sequences rather than accession numbers.

a4_units_stated.note: No units are stated because no measurement table exists. The script's output is a bare integer read count; converting that to an activity needs the unretrievable enrichment formula, and the 413x413 coupling matrix is a headerless numeric file with no units.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS badly. The mapping reference has exactly 9 constructs and the plasmid archive holds 9 designed variants plus wild type, so the experimentally characterised set is about 10 proteins. The absolute ceiling implied by the 54 design masks per lobe is roughly 108. Both are far under the 1,500-row threshold, and under the 400-row classification threshold.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 7 MB tarball; 2.2 GB if the raw reads were added
a6_fits_laptop.note: The design and mining files are trivially small for a laptop. Size is not what kills this candidate.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot be checked. The paper's full text and supplementary tables are not retrievable, so there is no stated screen size to compare the 9 deposited constructs against. 'High-throughput screening' in the abstract cannot be reconciled with 9 quantified constructs using only open sources.

a8_label_provenance.note: The only label available at scale would be circular. For the 20,000 unlabelled designs, the sole per-sequence score one could attach is the ESM-IF1 inverse-folding model's own likelihood, which is the model that generated them, so training on it distils that model rather than learning biology. The genuine physical measurement exists for only about 10 proteins.

existing_models.name: ProMEP (Protein Mutational Effect Predictor), a multimodal deep learning model trained on roughly 160 million proteins
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported in Cell Research (2024) as predicting mutation effects on the gene-editing enzyme TnpB with no task-specific training; a 5-site TnpB mutant it guided reached about 74% editing efficiency versus about 25% for wild type. Split details not retrieved.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved; I only read search summaries, not the paper itself.

backbone.name: ESM-2 (a protein language model) or ESM-IF1 (a structure-to-sequence inverse-folding model)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU would suffice for embedding 20,000 sequences of 408 amino acids, but there is nothing to fit a head against.
backbone.licence: MIT for the paper's own code; ESM weights are permissively licensed.

integration.partner_dataset: None usable. In principle the 1,501 mined TnpB homologues could join to UniProt and AlphaFold DB, but they carry contig coordinates and internal open-reading-frame identifiers rather than UniProt accessions.
integration.join_key: none present; identifiers are internal ORF numbers such as orf1005553 plus NCBI nucleotide contig accessions
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written, because no measured property exists in this deposit to join anything to.

controls.positive_control: Would be available in principle (recover sequence length or known catalytic-residue conservation from the sequences), but pointless without a label.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is not runnable: there are no labels to shuffle.
controls.external_validation: None. No second source reports activity for these specific designed variants, because they are non-natural proteins that exist only in this paper.

honest_claim_h3: With the deposited data the only honest claim is 'nine designed nucleases plus wild type were quantified in one assay', which is a wet-lab result, not a model's claim; no sequence-to-activity statement can be supported.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a designed nuclease's protein sequence to predict whether it still cuts DNA.
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered was: feed each designed variant's 408-amino-acid sequence (20,000 of them are deposited) to a protein language model and fit a small head. The fatal problem is that only about 10 of those 20,000 sequences have any measured activity.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a given designed variant retains DNA-cutting activity, and how strongly. The true answer would come from a bacterial survival screen in which an active nuclease destroys a toxic ccdB gene, read out by counting sequencing reads before and after selection.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups designing compact genome editors would love a cheap filter that ranks thousands of candidate designs before anyone clones them, since each tested design costs weeks of lab work. This dataset cannot support it.

more_or_better_data.why: ProMEP was trained on roughly 160 million proteins. This deposit offers about 10 activity measurements and 20,000 unlabelled sequences, so it is smaller by any measure that matters.

confidence_score.why: Per-prediction confidence needs replicate measurements across many items. Here the deposited quantification covers 9 constructs, which cannot estimate noise for a sequence-to-activity model.

models_beatable.why: ProMEP is a 2024 model already demonstrated on TnpB specifically, and there is no labelled test set here on which to beat it.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: there is no labelled training or evaluation set, so no baseline can be run and no comparison is possible.

ml_idea: The attractive-sounding project was to learn a sequence-to-activity model for artificially designed TnpB nucleases: embed each of the 20,000 deposited inverse-folding designs with ESM-2 and fit a head predicting ccdB-screen enrichment, giving a cheap pre-screen filter for compact genome editors. It is not buildable from this deposit, because the activity measurements were never tabulated and exist for only about 10 proteins. A salvageable but much smaller use of these files is purely descriptive: the 20,000 designs plus the 54 design masks document how far an inverse-folding model drifts from the wild-type sequence as its design constraints are loosened, which needs no labels but is a characterisation note, not an ML project.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed. The 40 hours covers downloading 2.12 GB of raw nanopore reads, installing minimap2 and running the authors' mapping script, then reverse-engineering the enrichment formula from a paywalled Methods section; it would still yield only 9 rows. The 6 embedding hours is a rough CPU estimate for 20,000 sequences of 408 amino acids through ESM-2, which is pointless here because those sequences have no labels.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the sequences in Reference_for_mapping.fasta and the plasmids in SynTnpB_HEK293T_plasmids.zip. I did this: 9 constructs and 9 variants plus wild type. That single count, which takes under a minute, kills the project outright.

verdict_reason: Fails A2, A5 and A8, all verified by opening the files. The deposit is a design-and-mining code release, not a measurement table: the 20,000 designed sequences carry no activity values, the only activity readout must be constructed from 2.12 GB of raw nanopore reads using an enrichment equation hidden behind the paywall, and the mapping reference plus the plasmid archive both show the experimentally characterised set is 9 designed variants plus wild type. The one label obtainable at scale would be the generating model's own likelihood, which is circular. The science is excellent and the data is openly licensed; there is simply no feature-and-label table here, and roughly 10 measured proteins is two orders of magnitude short of the threshold.
